scope: Every .cs file under src/RackCad.Application in the extract of commit 3375aadb (457 files; there are no obj/ or bin/ folders in the extract). Method: a Python pass flagged every line containing 'static' (skipping comments, static classes, 'using static', methods, operators and static lambdas), then I read each remaining hit. Separate regex passes looked for [ThreadStatic], ThreadLocal, AsyncLocal, static events, ModuleInitializer, static constructors, static properties with set/init, volatile, Lazy, lock objects, AppDomain and Registry use. Negative findings (FACT): no static constructors, no module initializers, no static events, no ThreadStatic/ThreadLocal/AsyncLocal, and no static properties with a setter. Only one static field is not readonly: RackLog.sink. No static initializer does file, registry or AppDomain I/O. The only one that reads the environment is RackLog.cs:18 (Environment.GetFolderPath, RackLog.cs:67-68). To check reachability I read the Plugin seam files: RackSelectivoCommands, SelectiveFrontalDrawService/SelectivePlantaDrawService, ViewBlockDraw, SystemBlockWriter, BlockLibraryImporter, RackCatalogLoader, RackBlockFinder and RackCommandSupport.

entries.warmup_risk: HIGH relevance, LOW behavioural effect. The key is the catalog directory path, not the side database or drawing. After a warm-up, the governed run gets the SAME RackCatalog object by reference (:79-81) as long as no csv/json in that folder changed name, size or mtime tick. Parsing, CSV reads and Latin-1 fallback decoding are skipped (timing differs; content is the same). This only stays equivalent while no consumer mutates the shared catalog. FACT: grep found no reassignment of any RackCatalog list property and no 'Defaults.X =' in Application, Plugin or UI. Mutation of individual entries is UNCERTAIN. An edit between the two runs that keeps the same length and mtime tick would be missed (UNCERTAIN, depends on filesystem timestamp resolution).

limitations: This census covers src/RackCad.Application only. The Plugin layer holds non-readonly static state directly on the library-import seam that I did not analyze: Plugin/Drawing/BlockLibraryDatabaseCache.cs:11-15 (CacheGate, cachedPath, cachedWriteUtc, cachedLength, cachedLibrary, a side Database acquired at BlockLibraryImporter.cs:96 and AutoCadExternalLibraryBlockQuery.cs:27). It is probably the largest warm-up carrier, and a separate Plugin census is needed.

Some effects come from framework behavior, not from repo code, and are marked UNCERTAIN: System.Text.Json freezing options and caching type metadata on first use, and beforefieldinit type-initialization timing (there are no explicit static constructors, so initializers run at or before first static-field access).

I established that the shared RackCatalog (cache) and RackFrameTemplate (All) objects are not mutated by grepping for property assignments, collection mutators and downcasts in Application, Plugin and UI. This is not a full data-flow proof: mutation of individual catalog entries and indirect mutation stay UNCERTAIN.

Reachability is scoped to the Selective CREATE path (RACKSELECTIVO -> DrawSelectiveView). The WPF RackSelectiveWindow that RACKSELECTIVO opens first is outside the listed seam but reaches the same JsonRackCatalogProvider cache (RackCad.UI/UiSupport.cs:88). Whether a warm-up opens that window is unknown. The edit and update paths (RackSelectivoCommands.EditSelective :48-160) reach additional state (ProjectVariablesStore, SelectiveLinkedProperties, SelectiveEditorOpen.NoStates) that I marked NO.

The durable on-disk effects I report (appends to the daily log file; quarantining a corrupt settings.json to .bad) are not static memory state. I included them because they carry over from a warm-up into a governed run.

The first pass used a line-based classifier and regex. I then checked multi-line declarations, generic tuple types and CRLF-terminated lines by hand and with a comment-stripped regex pass over whole files. None of those passes found any declaration the classifier had missed.
